invariants.statement: A missing value becomes `nil`.
A null value becomes `nil`.
A number JSON cannot carry becomes the Lua expression for that number.
An array becomes a Lua table keyed by position.
An object becomes a Lua table keyed by string.
A value no Lua literal can have is refused rather than dropped.
A long literal is fenced with the equals signs the text forces.
Nothing here runs a process.

value.definition: a number written the way Lua 5.1 writes that number

invariants.statement: A whole number is written with no fractional part.
Every other number is written to fourteen significant digits.
Seventeen digits are used where fourteen lose the number.
A trailing zero of a fraction is dropped.
An exponent is written with a sign and at least two digits.

value.definition: the sentinels and the answer shape the driver and its caller agree on

invariants.statement: The sentinels are written once here and read by both sides.
An answer is parsed rather than trusted.
A tagged object naming a number JSON cannot have becomes that number.
A tagged object naming a function is left tagged and frozen.
Nothing here runs a process.

value.definition: a Lua subprocess handed out as something to run scripts on and read globals from

invariants.statement: A script that fails throws the error Lua gave rather than answering.
A global is read by running a return of that global's name.
Stubs the caller hands in are loaded before the caller gets the VM.
Stubs that fail to load close the subprocess rather than leaving the subprocess half set up.

value.definition: a Lua subprocess started, handed scripts one at a time, and shut down

invariants.statement: The subprocess loads the driver from the file beside the driver's own page.
A start is proved by a handshake script whose answer is known beforehand.
A handshake that hangs is given a deadline rather than waited on.
A start that fails is tried again a fixed number of times.
A failure names the subprocess and the work the subprocess did before failing.
The bytes the subprocess wrote to its error stream are kept for that report.
Only the last four kilobytes of the error stream are kept.
A script handed to a closed subprocess is refused.
Closing ends the subprocess input and waits for the subprocess to exit.

value.definition: a Lua VM whose globals answer as the game's globals would

invariants.statement: The prelude is loaded from the file beside the prelude's own page.
The prelude file is read once and kept for every VM after the first.
The banned names are handed over before the prelude loads.
A seeded value waits until the next source is loaded.
A seeded value no Lua literal can carry is seeded as a stub instead.
A seeded function is seeded as a stub.
Source is handed over as one long literal rather than as an escaped string.

value.definition: whether a value that may be a callback is one rather than a plain value
